rv.q: This is a show of wonder and delight, and after its West End run it tours nationally until May.
It has immediacy, and a ramshackle liveliness that is enormously appealing.

Helen Edmundson’s book is a charming adventure complimented by Robert Innes Hopkins quirky design and if Neil Hannon’s songs sometimes sit a little awkwardly in the narrative, you will probably be too busy having fun to notice that much.
Its hugely appealing good humor and heart deserve a return engagement at the very least.
Morris succeeds in charming all who sail in her.

cn.t: This captivating adaptation delights audiences with its inventive staging and fresh take on Arthur Ransome's classic tale, celebrating the power of childhood imagination through funny, affecting storytelling that proves perfect family entertainment.
